question: A shopkeeper marks his goods at 20% above the cost price. He sells 40% of the goods at the marked price and the remaining at 30% discount on the marked price. His gain/loss percentage is:
solution:
Given:

A shopkeeper marks his goods at 20% above the cost price.

He sells 40% of the goods at the marked price and the remaining at 30% discount on the marked price.

Concept used:

Loss% = {(Cost Price - Selling Price) over Cost Price} times 100\%

Marked Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Rise%

Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 - Discount%)

Calculation:

Let there be N number of goods and cost price of each good be Q.

So, the market price = Q + Q × 20%

⇒ 1.2Q 

The total cost price of the goods = QN

The selling price of 40% of the goods = 1.2Q × N × 40%

⇒ 0.48NQ

Discounted selling price = 1.2Q - 1.2Q × 30%

⇒ 1.2Q - 0.36Q = 0.84Q

The selling price of the remaining goods = 0.84Q × N × (100 - 40)%

⇒ 0.504NQ

The total selling price of the goods

⇒ 0.504NQ + 0.48NQ

⇒ 0.984Q

Now, loss% = {{NQ - 0.984Q} over NQ} times 100\%

⇒ 0.016 times 100\% = 1.6%

∴ His loss percentage is 1.6%.
